items.author: Bryan Johnson
items.text:
New plasma proteome panel reads insulin resistance better than standard lab tests

Metabolic decline evades early detection because the body works overtime to keep standard markers looking normal. 

13 proteins plus basic health metrics outperformed standard clinical tests at predicting insulin resistance and 10 yr risk for fatty liver and obesity.

Also cool that proteins picked up a 30%+ improvement in insulin sensitivity post 8 weeks of HIIT.

items.author: J.K. Lundblad | Teaching Progress
items.text:
ApoStructura is correct.

One of my favorite essay on this subject is on R&P.

I charted the progress in transport speeds here:

It should be noted that the breakthrough in transport come in pulses; as one mode begins to decline, the other rises.

Also worth mentioning that the total size of the network grows larger than the last, opening more corners of the world.

Also, my favorite fact: the faster the transportation mode, the higher the value items transported.

Ships and rail, for instance, move raw materials, trucks move intermediate goods, and aircraft high value consumer goods.

quoted.author: ApoStructura
quoted.text:
Before the horse you couldn’t travel more than 20km a day, then horses tripled that, trains/cars/ships added 10x more, and finally another 10x with planes to 10,000km.

Space travel will bring the next 10x leap, and nuclear electric the following 10x.

Mars won’t feel far then.
